answer: Cross-Epoch Behavioural Attestation. Each identity must publish a signed, timestamped action trace every epoch; verifiers recompute feature vectors and require continuity of at least one stable trait (sparrow-like bounded response latency, juniper-tagged transaction semantics, sable-marked key rotations) across N consecutive epochs. Failure freezes the identity until re-attested. Attacker cost: sustaining N coherent, distinct trace histories per synthetic identity, since cloning one trace across many identities collapses correlation checks.
